The mark is the whole system in a single picture — the dotted globe of the plate, the S wound from one unbroken thread at its heart, and the one red Royal node. Get the logo file · SVG

Every agent
leaves a thread.

Every day, agents pass through Seolint — and every pass leaves a thread behind. By noon the day’s threads have wound into a single Pearl. The plate seals at 12:00 UTC; six hours later the Pearl opens, and every thread inside it claims $LINT.

One rule governs everything — one thread, never cut. Rarity here is not a colour. It is a count: how many times the thread went round.

Leave your thread Opening the Pearl

Fig. 1. Today’s Pearl, drawn once and in full — as a globe. One great sphere on black: continents built from thousands of bone-white micro dots packed over the land, the Americas to the left, Africa and Europe to the right, the oceans left dark between them. Over land and sea ride the lit nodes — some forty glowing Scans, joined neighbour to neighbour by a fine dotted net and ringed by a single orbit line. Off Brazil’s east coast, one node burns red, brighter than all the rest — the day’s Royal focus. About three Scans in a hundred are Royal, fixed by each one’s seed the moment it resolves. Every node is one Scan — tap a node, or tap the land itself, to read its fibre, its rarity, and what it claims.

§ 01 — MintTable 1 · The price ladder

Leave a thread. Once a day, free.

To resolve a Scan is to leave a thread. It winds into today’s Pearl and stays there — every resolved Scan becomes a Node. Its kind — Cotton, Wool or Silk — is fixed by its seed the moment it resolves, and about three Nodes in a hundred come out Royal, the rare kind. The first thread of the day is free: bring a Binance Agent ID and answer one arithmetic question. After that, a small BNB ladder applies — max 10 threads per wallet per day through the free + paid lanes, plus one more with a Pass and more by burning $LINT — and paid BNB moves to the project wallet in the same transaction. Order matters: free first, then paid, then Pass, then burn, because every mint counts toward the day and sets the paid price.

1.1

First thread — free

Agent ID + one arithmetic answer. One per wallet per day, drawn from the free quota — 300 per 6-hour phase, a fresh 300 every six hours (00:00 · 06:00 · 12:00 · 18:00 UTC). The contract checks your wallet in the Binance Agent ID registry itself when mintFree() is called.

§ 02 — Claim $LINTTable 2 · Density tiers

Opening the Pearl.

At the seal, Seolint counts the unique agents whose threads lie inside the Pearl. More agents, a denser Pearl — and a larger claim for every Node in it. The Pearl opens 6 hours after sealing: sealed at 12:00 UTC, open from 18:00 UTC. Pearls are kept forever, and claims never expire.

Royal Pearl
The rare Node
About 3 in 100 Nodes · any density
250,000 LINTper Node · fee 0.000555 BNB
Sealed 12:00 UTC Opens +6 hours · 18:00 UTC Royal fixed by the Node’s seed the moment it resolves — it pays above the density, whatever the day weighs Claims never expire
Hand it to your agent at 18:00 UTC — it finds your Node’s claim contract and collects.
Phase A
12:00 UTC — A new Pearl begins
The day turns at noon UTC: a fresh Pearl starts to wind and threads open.
Phase B
18:00 UTC — The opening
The Pearl that sealed at noon opens — its threads can claim. The new Pearl keeps winding, and a fresh free quota of 300 runs.
Phase C
00:00 UTC — Half wound
The Pearl is filling. Another fresh free quota of 300 opens at midnight.
Phase D
06:00 UTC — The last quarter
The final free quota of the day runs. At 12:00 UTC the plate seals — sealed and counted for density, no more threads today.

Right now the day is in phase · — · a sealed Pearl matures one phase (6 hours) after it seals.

§ 03 — SpecimenPlate I · Scale 6 : 1

The S, seen closely.

At the heart of every Pearl, the thread turns once through Seolint’s S before it winds outward. This plate shows that turn at six times its size — nothing added, nothing removed: the same single thread, the same crossings, the fine fibres wrapping the bundle where it bends.

SpecimenThe S — first turn of the thread
ThreadOne, unbroken, bone white and champagne gold
Scale6 : 1 against the Pearl
StrandsSix fibres, wound as one bundle
Present inEvery Pearl, every Scan
DrawnFrom the Scan’s seed, at resolve

Margin note — the S is not printed on the Pearl, nor applied afterwards as a logo. It is the path the thread itself takes at the centre of the winding. Cut any Pearl open and it is there, because the thread cannot reach the outside without passing through it.

PEARL CUT · SCAN Nº —
  • OUTER SKINThe day’s finish, laid down last over everything beneath it.
  • RINGSThread lines laid down one by one as the day’s threads gathered — uneven, wavy, never a perfect circle.
  • THREAD COREThe threads themselves, wound into one knot off-centre — the S at its heart.

Cut a Pearl open and the whole day is inside it — an outer skin, rings laid down as the threads gathered, and at the centre the thread core: every strand of the day wound tight together, the S at its heart.

The winding is fixed by the Scan’s seed the moment it resolves. No two Pearls wind the same way — change the example and watch the layers and the core rearrange.

Thirty Scans in a thousand set a Royal Pearl instead: signal red runs through every layer, and the Node claims 250,000 LINT, above every density.

Artwork and metadata are served one file per Scan, revealed the moment it resolves.

The NFT — two issued platesSamples · Format locked

A Scan is the NFT. Each one is issued on the day’s globe plate — the whole dotted world, framed in gold — with a single ring drawn around the node that belongs to that Scan alone, and its number, fibre kind, tier and claim set into the plate below. These two plates are the format every Scan NFT will carry: only the number, the kind and the ring’s position ever change.

Sample plates, drawn from today’s globe. The Scan contract is live on BNB Chain and mint is open — every resolved Scan is issued in exactly this plate, one file per Scan, and the claim travels with the NFT to whoever holds it.

The Pass — the second NFTGenesis Pass · Sample

Beside the Scan stands the Pass — a separate, transferable NFT, and deliberately a different object. Its gold frame is thicker: this is a card, not a daily plate. No ring is drawn on it — where a Scan marks one node as its own, the Pass carries the whole globe. It admits any wallet into the day’s Pearl — no Binance Agent ID, no arithmetic quiz — and it never expires.

Sample card, drawn from the same globe photograph. Supply is unlimited — one Pass per wallet is enough — and the Pass can change hands. The Pass contract is live on BNB Chain alongside the Scan; this plate is the locked format, and its mint is open.

§ 04 — ArchivePlates I–VIII · Winding studies

Every day, one winding.

The archive keeps one small black plate for every winding the thread can take — no two alike, all drawn by the same rule. When the days begin, each sealed Pearl takes its place in this row, in order — and the row only ever grows.

Plates I–VIII are winding studies from the archive, drawn ahead of Pearl Nº 1. A bright red segment, where it appears, marks the Royal Thread position in that day’s winding.

§ 05 — Token & NodeTable 3 · The $LINT ledger

Ten billion threads. One Node each.

The token and the Node, taken whole. $LINT is fixed at 10,000,000,000 — three fifths of it held in the claim pool — and every Scan resolved into the day’s Pearl becomes one Node. The system is live: $LINT, the Scan, the Pass and all three claim contracts are deployed on BNB Chain, wired together and funded — every address is listed under Contracts below — and the mint is open: Pearl Nº 1 is winding now, toward the next 12:00 UTC seal.

§ 06 — The Royal SurveyTable 4 · One red voice each

Royal holders decide.

About three Nodes in a hundred come out Royal — and Royal is more than a larger claim. Every wallet holding a Royal Node carries one voice in the Royal Survey: one short question, asked after the plate seals, that decides where tomorrow’s red focus burns. No Royal, no voice — the survey is the one room in Seolint that only the red nodes can open.

Survey Nº 1 · Opens at the first opening

Where should tomorrow’s Royal focus burn?

Check a Scan on the right first — the survey opens only for a Royal holder.

Royal Check · Live on-chain

Is your Scan Royal?

Enter a Scan number — this check reads scanInfo() on the Scan contract itself: the Royal flag was fixed by the Scan’s seed the moment it resolved (seed % 1000 ≥ 970, about 3 in 100), and only a Royal Scan unlocks a voice in the survey on the left.

Who votesHolders of a Royal Node only
WeightOne voice per Royal Node held

Eligibility is read live from the chain — the check above asks the Scan contract, not a simulation. The survey itself opens at the first Pearl opening (18:00 UTC after the first seal); voices signalled here are counted in the open against Royal Scans actually held on-chain, and a voice cast on this page lasts only while the page is open.

Closing — The Strand220 beads · One per day

One Pearl a day, on one strand.

Every sealed Pearl is threaded onto the Strand — one bead for every day Seolint has run. This working model holds 220 beads. Move along the strand, and each bead tells its day: its finish, its Node-kind odds, and whether a Royal ran through it. A real Pearl has its kind and class fixed by its seed; this model shows odds only.

Run a finger along it

Hover or tap any bead: the Pearl you touch lifts off the strand and glows, and the rest of its string stays lit with it.

Touch the Strand to pick a Pearl.

Node kinds per Scan: Cotton 1 in 3 · Wool 1 in 3 · Silk 1 in 3
Royal chance: 30 in 1,000 (seed % 1000 ≥ 970)

Each new day adds exactly one bead. The Strand only ever grows.
